keyVerseText: Of the tribe of Joseph, namely, of the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi the son of Susi.
rootMeaning: The root word גָּדִי (Gâdîy) means "my fortune," and גַּדִּי (Gaddîy) is an intensive form of this root, emphasizing the sense of personal possession or blessing. This intensification suggests a deeper or more pronounced sense of one's own fortune or blessing, which is reflected in the personal name. The name thus carries connotations of divine favor or providential blessing bestowed upon the individual, beyond a mere label.
usageInScripture: The term גַּדִּי (Gaddîy) appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Numbers 13:11, where it is used as a proper name referring to an Israelite from the tribe of Manasseh. The consistent translation as "Gaddi" across its single occurrence highlights its function as a personal name rather than a common noun, underscoring the importance of individual identity within the tribal and covenantal context of Israel.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding גַּדִּי (Gaddîy) as meaning "my fortune" enriches our appreciation of biblical names as carriers of divine purpose and blessing. The fact that Gaddi was a spy sent by Moses to survey Canaan connects the idea of "fortune" with God's providential guidance in the conquest of the Promised Land. This reminds believers that their lives and missions are encompassed by God's sovereign blessing and purpose. It encourages faith that God’s favor is personal and intentional, shaping the course of His people’s history in fulfillment of His promises through Christ.
keyVerseReflection: Numbers 13:11 identifies Gaddi as "the son of Susi" from the tribe of Manasseh, emphasizing his role within the community of Israel. The use of the name Gaddi here not only marks an individual but also subtly conveys the idea of being under God's providential blessing as he participates in the crucial mission to scout the land God promised. This reinforces the trustworthiness of God's promises and the assurance that His chosen people are guided by His sovereign hand.
